evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Before I go over the information besides pricing, do you have any questions or concerns you would like answered on this call? [Asked after name/phone/email already confirmed, but before main probing started]
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Rep asked follow-up on gym equipment concern: 'For that weight to, does it have like holes and things like that' and continued clarifying: 'Oh, okay. Like the rack. Okay, la rack.' Also asked about the large monitor and got additional detail. Went back to confirm the inventory list.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: A typical move this size takes two movers and one truck between two and a half and four hours... I would look to estimate between three and four hours for your move. And then I would look to budget between $699 and $907... includes a $75 trip fee
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' Instead ended with 'I'm gonna send this email out' and transitioned directly to confirmation without a plain ask for the business.

top_strength: Brianne gathered exhaustive logistics details and special considerations (gym equipment, TV, monitor, all furniture pieces, exact item counts) through methodical probing, creating a comprehensive inventory that protects estimate accuracy.
coaching_note: Section 1 is missing the foundational quid pro quo framing (time-boxed promise + dependable quote + wait for yes), and Section 7 never includes an explicit ask for the business—both are load-bearing close gaps that prevent the customer from committing.
